_comment: THE ROAD CLASS TABLE (ADR-0276, moved here from C++ by ADR-0438; issue #292). A road class is a kind of road: a local
street, an arterial, a freeway, a ramp, a railway track, a footway. Each row says what a road of that class is made
of across its width, how steeply it may climb, and how the builder treats it. This file is the one home of those
facts. It is read once (src/engine/procgen/city/roads/lanes/road_graph_spec.cpp roadClasses). A level's road file
may state its own `classes` on top: a class it names starts from the row of that name here (or, a name this table
does not have, from the `default` row with no kerb parking), and each key it writes replaces that row's value.
Nothing in the code asks a class by its name: a behaviour that depends on the class is a key of its row.
THE KEYS OF A ROW (the same keys a road file's `classes` uses):
like              start from another row of this table, then apply this row's keys (the mountain road is the rural
road graded differently). Only in this file.
w                 the width of one travel lane, metres.
fwd, back         travel lanes running along the road's centre line, and against it. back 0: a one-way road.
gap               the strip between the two ways of a two-way road, metres (default 0).
parking           kerb parking: a band this wide along each kerb, over the kerb side of the kerb lane (default 0).
shoulder          paved shoulder outside the lanes each side, metres.
sidewalk          sidewalk outside that each side, metres.
median            a divider's own width, metres (only the divider row).
rank              which road wins where two meet: the higher rank keeps its height and owns shared pavement.
g_max             the steepest grade it may climb (0.08 is 8 %).
window            metres over which its height profile is smoothed.
thick             how thick its deck is where it stands on a bridge, metres.
balance           0: the road only fills (rides over a dip); 0.5: it also cuts through a rise (default 0).
track             true: its lanes are railway tracks. No car, walker or building uses it as a street.
footway           true: a paved path for people on foot. No car drives it.
junction_markings false: no crosswalk, stop bar or lane arrow is painted where it meets a junction (default true).
frontage          "none": no building faces it -- no lot's door, walk or plaza along it, and no door is answered
with it (a freeway, a ramp, a mountain pass between towns). "both" (default): any building may.
engine_class      which of the engine's six driving classes it is for routing, speed and the map: local, collector,
arterial, freeway, ramp or alley (default local). A road laid as a ramp (anchored to a host
road's lane) is always a ramp, whatever its class says.
limited_access    true: a road other roads never meet at one level (a freeway). Where it crosses any road but a
ramp, one of the two is carried over on a bridge; two of them side by side share a median wall;
a road that is not one, running close beside it, gets a noise wall (default false).
default_barriers  true: its edges carry the builder's usual walls and guardrails where this row's `edges` does
not say otherwise (a freeway, a ramp). false: only what `edges` states (default false).
plan_colour       the fill its lanes are drawn with on the plan picture lanes_tool writes (default #3a3a3c).
edges             the barrier along its edge, by where the edge is: seam (against other pavement), median, vs_street
(a street close beside), elevated (on a bridge), at_grade. Each: kind none | wall | guardrail,
h (height), thick, offset (out from the edge), min_drop (only where the ground falls this far).
A place not listed gets the builder's usual barrier where default_barriers is true, else none.
WHY THE NUMBERS. The sections are the default city brief's (12 / 16 / 22 / 30 m carriageways, 5 m sidewalks), so an
arterial's lane is 22 / 6 m. The grades are the planner's: a freeway 6 %, an arterial or a boulevard 8 %, a collector
or a rural road 10 %, a local street 12 %, a ramp 9 % (with 8 % the diamonds on a hilly ring ran longer than the
535 m between its arterials), a mountain road 15 % (at the rural 10 % the island pass rode a 2.5 km viaduct).
A local street parks along both kerbs: 2.5 m of its 6 m lane each way (ADR-0418). The rural road's 2.5 m shoulder
is a ramp's (Glenn, 2026-11-04: the two-lane mountain roads were too narrow to drive). The mountain road has
guardrails on its bridges, and at grade only where the ground 5 m out drops 2 m or more (ADR-0117). A railway is a
double track at 4 m centres graded 2.5 %; light rail 3.6 m centres and 5 %; both walled where they stand on a bridge.
A footway is one 3 m path, walled wherever it stands clear of the ground; steeper than 15 % it is built as steps.
